# Rainman Translate Book [![English (current language)](https://img.shields.io/badge/English-e9c13f)](#rainman-translate-book) [![Read in Chinese (中文)](https://img.shields.io/badge/%E4%B8%AD%E6%96%87-1f6b52)](README.zh-CN.md) [![Read in Japanese (日本語)](https://img.shields.io/badge/%E6%97%A5%E6%9C%AC%E8%AA%9E-1f6b52)](README.ja.md) [![Project page: translate.dyu.sh/en, a one-page guide](https://img.shields.io/badge/Project_page-translate.dyu.sh%2Fen_%C2%B7_a_one--page_guide-e9c13f?labelColor=1f6b52)](https://translate.dyu.sh/en/) An Agent Skill for Claude Code, Codex, Cursor, OpenClaw and other Agent Skills–compatible agents that translates entire books (PDF/DOCX/EPUB) into any language using parallel subagents.

> Inspired by [claude_translater](https://github.com/wizlijun/claude_translater). The original project uses shell scripts as its entry point, coordinating the Claude CLI with multiple step scripts to perform chunked translation. This project restructures the workflow as an Agent Skill for Claude Code, Codex, Cursor, OpenClaw, and other compatible agents, using subagents to translate chunks in parallel, with manifest-driven integrity checks, resumable runs, and multi-format output unified into a single pipeline. As the project structure and implementation differ significantly from the original, this is an independent project rather than a fork. --- ## How It Works ``` Input (PDF/DOCX/EPUB) │ ▼ Calibre ebook-convert → HTMLZ → HTML → Markdown (or Markdown from a layout-aware PDF parser, skipping Calibre) │ ▼ Split into chunks (chunk0001.md, chunk0002.md, ...) │ manifest.json tracks chunk hashes ▼ Parallel subagents (8 concurrent by default) │ each subagent: read 1 chunk → translate → write output_chunk*.md │ batched to respect API rate limits ▼ Validate (manifest hash check, 1:1 source↔output match) │ ▼ Merge → Pandoc → HTML (with TOC) → Calibre → DOCX / EPUB / PDF ``` Each chunk gets its own independent subagent with a fresh context window. This prevents context accumulation and output truncation that happen when translating a full book in a single session. ## Features - **Parallel subagents** — 8 concurrent translators per batch, each with isolated context - **Resumable + selective re-translation** — chunk-level resume, with `run_state.json` tracking glossary-sensitive re-translation - **Neighbor context** — each chunk can see short read-only excerpts from adjacent chunks for pronoun and entity resolution - **Manifest validation** — SHA-256 hash tracking prevents stale or corrupt outputs from being merged - **Multi-format output** — HTML (with floating TOC), DOCX, EPUB, PDF - **Optional output controls** — explicit EPUB cover, custom temp root, and user-facing export aliases - **Multi-language** — any language code, e.g. zh, en, ja, ko, fr, de, es, it (Italian), or one with a region such as zh-TW or pt-BR - **PDF/DOCX/EPUB/Markdown input** — Calibre handles the conversion heavy lifting; formula- and table-heavy PDFs can be pre-extracted to Markdown with a layout-aware parser (see [Step 1](#step-1-convert)) ## Prerequisites - **Agent runtime** — any agent that supports Agent Skills and can launch sub-agents from a skill (see [Compatibility](#compatibility)) - **Calibre** — `ebook-convert` command must be available ([download](https://calibre-ebook.com/)) - **Pandoc** — for HTML↔Markdown conversion ([download](https://pandoc.org/)) - **Python 3** with: - `pypandoc` — optional (`pip install pypandoc`); without it the `pandoc` binary is called directly - `beautifulsoup4` — optional, for better TOC generation (`pip install beautifulsoup4`) - **A layout-aware PDF parser** — optional, only to pre-extract formula- and table-heavy PDFs to Markdown; supported parsers are listed in [Step 1](#step-1-convert) ## Quick Start ### 1. Install the skill #### Any Agent Skills–compatible agent ```bash npx skills add deusyu/translate-book ``` The command asks which agents to install the skill for. To install it globally for one agent, pass `-a -g`, for example `npx skills add deusyu/translate-book -a cursor -g`: | `-a` | Installed to | |------|--------------| | `claude-code` | `~/.claude/skills/translate-book` | | `codex`, `cursor`, `gemini-cli`, `opencode`, `github-copilot` | `~/.agents/skills/translate-book` (shared) | | `antigravity` | `~/.gemini/config/skills/translate-book` | | `openclaw` | `~/.openclaw/skills/translate-book` | Or install it manually: ```bash mkdir -p ~/.agents/skills git clone https://github.com/deusyu/translate-book.git ~/.agents/skills/translate-book ``` Codex, Cursor, Gemini CLI, OpenCode, and GitHub Copilot read `~/.agents/skills/`. For Claude Code, clone into `~/.claude/skills/translate-book` instead. Restart the agent if the newly installed skill does not appear. #### Plugin marketplace (Claude Code, GitHub Copilot CLI) In Claude Code: ```text /plugin marketplace add deusyu/translate-book /plugin install translate-book@translate-book ``` In GitHub Copilot CLI: ```bash copilot plugin marketplace add deusyu/translate-book copilot plugin install translate-book@translate-book ``` Install the skill either as a plugin or into a skills directory, not both: an agent that finds both copies loads both. In Claude Code, the plugin's skill is invoked as `/translate-book:translate-book`. #### OpenClaw ```bash openclaw skills install @deusyu/translate-book ``` ### 2. Translate a book #### Codex In the Codex CLI or IDE extension, enter: ```text $translate-book Translate /path/to/book.pdf into Chinese. ``` Codex can also select the skill automatically when your request matches its description. #### Other agents Ask the agent: ```text translate /path/to/book.pdf to Chinese ``` In Claude Code and Cursor, you can also use the slash command: ```text /translate-book translate /path/to/book.pdf to Japanese ``` In OpenCode, mention `@translate-book` in the request. The skill handles the full pipeline automatically — convert, chunk, translate in parallel, validate, merge, and build all output formats. ### 3. Find your outputs All files are in `{book_name}_temp/`: | File | Description | |------|-------------| | `output.md` | Merged translated Markdown | | `book.html` | Web version with floating TOC | | `book.docx` | Word document | | `book.epub` | E-book | | `book.pdf` | Print-ready PDF | ## Compatibility The skill needs an agent that can launch sub-agents from a skill, one per chunk. If the agent cannot, the skill says so and stops instead of translating the whole book in a single context. | Agent | Status | Invoke | |-------|--------|--------| | Cursor | Verified | `/translate-book`, or describe the task | | Claude Code | Original host; minimal test not yet re-run | `/translate-book` (plugin install: `/translate-book:translate-book`), or describe the task | | Codex | Verified | `$translate-book`, or describe the task | | OpenClaw | Original host; minimal test not yet re-run | Describe the task | | Antigravity | Installable, not yet verified | Describe the task | | Gemini CLI | Installable, not yet verified | Describe the task | | OpenCode | Installable, not yet verified | `@translate-book`, or describe the task | | GitHub Copilot | Installable, not yet verified | Describe the task | "Verified" means the agent passed this minimal test. Install the skill, then convert a baseline book that ships with it: ```bash S=~/.agents/skills/translate-book # the skill's install directory mkdir -p /tmp/tb-smoke && cd /tmp/tb-smoke python3 "$S/scripts/convert.py" "$S/tests/baselines/diligent-dick/diligent-dick.epub" --olang zh ``` Then ask the agent: ```text Use the translate-book skill. Do not convert again; the temp directory is /tmp/tb-smoke/diligent-dick_temp. Only handle chunk0045 and chunk0046, concurrency=2, skip the glossary step, launch one sub-agent per chunk as in Step 4 of SKILL.md to translate them into Chinese, and stop when done. ``` The agent passes when all three hold: 1. The transcript shows `python3 /absolute/path/scripts/chunk_context.py …`, so `{baseDir}` was resolved to a real path. 2. The write times of `diligent-dick_temp/output_chunk0045*` and `output_chunk0046*` overlap with the other sub-agent's run, so the chunks were translated in parallel rather than one after another by the main agent. 3. `python3 "$S/scripts/merge_meta.py" status diligent-dick_temp` reports `malformed_meta_files: 0`. Ran it on an agent that is not marked Verified? Please open an issue with the agent, its version, and the three results. ## Repository Test Assets - Checked-in baseline inputs live under `tests/baselines//`. - Generated full-pipeline outputs live under `tests/.artifacts/` and should not be committed. - Because `scripts/convert.py` writes `{book_name}_temp/` under the current working directory, run repository baseline tests from inside `tests/.artifacts/` to keep generated files out of the repo root. ### Full-Pipeline Baseline Example ```bash mkdir -p tests/.artifacts cd tests/.artifacts python3 ../../scripts/convert.py ../baselines/standard-alice/standard-alice.epub --olang zh # then run translation via the skill python3 ../../scripts/merge_and_build.py --temp-dir standard-alice_temp --title "test" ``` ## Feedback and Contributions Please open a detailed GitHub issue instead of starting with a pull request. This project is maintained as an AI-assisted skill pipeline, and changes need to be evaluated against the current orchestration rules, chunk/manifest contracts, baseline assets, and release flow in one maintainer-owned context. Pull requests are not the preferred contribution path and may be closed in favor of an issue. If you already have a patch, include the idea, key diff, failing case, or verification notes in the issue; the maintainer may rework or split the implementation before merging. A useful issue should include: - Current behavior and expected behavior - Input format and environment, such as PDF/DOCX/EPUB, OS, Python, Calibre, and Pandoc versions - Minimal reproduction steps or a small public-domain sample when possible - Logs, screenshots, or generated file names that show the failure ## Contact For bugs and feature requests, please open a [GitHub issue](https://github.com/deusyu/translate-book/issues) as described above. For questions, ideas, or anything else, you can reach me here: | Channel | Link | |---------|------| | X (Twitter) | [@0xdeusyu](https://x.com/0xdeusyu) | | Telegram | [@DeusThink](https://t.me/DeusThink) | | Telegram Group (Chinese) | [@talkdeusyu](https://t.me/talkdeusyu) | | Telegram Channel (Chinese) | [@lovedesuyu](https://t.me/lovedesuyu) | | Email | [rainman.deus@gmail.com](mailto:rainman.deus@gmail.com) | For commercial sponsorship, see [Commercial sponsorship](#commercial-sponsorship) below. The channel is my running log of thinking alongside AI; the group is its discussion space, and translate-book questions are welcome there too. ## Pipeline Details ### Step 1: Convert ```bash python3 scripts/convert.py /path/to/book.pdf --olang zh ``` Calibre converts the input to HTMLZ, which is extracted and converted to Markdown, then split into chunks (~6000 chars each). A `manifest.json` records the SHA-256 hash of each source chunk for later validation, and a `source_fingerprint.json` ties the temp dir to the exact source bytes it was built from — re-running against a replaced source file aborts instead of silently reusing stale chunks. Temp dirs created before fingerprinting are adopted with a warning on first re-run. The HTML → Markdown step also cleans Calibre's markup structurally. EPUB footnotes — a marker link such as `1` in the text, paired with a note paragraph that opens with a link back to it — become Pandoc footnotes (`[^1]` in the text, `[^1]: …` right after the paragraph), numbered across the whole book so that per-chapter numbering cannot collide after merging. In-book links keep their text, span attributes such as `{lang="…"}`, empty page anchors, and heading ids are dropped, and typographic dashes and quotes stay as Unicode instead of `---` or escaped ASCII quotes. Notes without a back-link (for example EPUB 3 `
` footnotes) stay ordinary paragraphs. By default the working directory is `{book_name}_temp/` under the current directory. Use `--temp-root /path/to/work` to keep the same leaf directory name under a different parent. #### Formula- and table-heavy PDFs: convert Markdown instead (optional) Calibre reflows PDF text by coordinate heuristics. That works for plain prose, but academic and technical PDFs lose their structure: formulas break into fragments, tables flatten into one cell per line, and multi-column pages interleave. For those PDFs, extract them with a layout-aware parser first and give `convert.py` the Markdown it writes. `.md` / `.markdown` input skips Calibre entirely: ```bash mineru-kit parse paper.pdf -o paper.md # or any parser from the table below python3 scripts/convert.py paper.md --olang zh ``` Any parser works if its Markdown follows these conventions: - **Formulas** as `$...$` / `$$...$$` LaTeX. Display-math blocks are never split across chunks. - **Tables** as Markdown pipe tables or HTML ``. - **Images** as files in the Markdown file's directory or its subdirectories, or inlined as base64 data URIs. `convert.py` copies or decodes them into `{book_name}_temp/images/`, so chunks never carry image payloads. An image whose path leads outside that directory (through `..`, an absolute path, or a symlink) is not copied: `convert.py` warns and leaves the reference as it is. | Parser | Install | Extract | Markdown file | Notes | |---|---|---|---|---| | [MinerU](https://github.com/opendatalab/MinerU) >= 4 | `pip install -U "mineru>=4.0,<5"` | `mineru-kit parse paper.pdf -o paper.md` | `paper.md` | CPU-only basic tier: ~0.8 GB of models | | [Marker](https://github.com/datalab-to/marker) | `pip install marker-pdf` | `marker_single paper.pdf --output_dir out/` | `out/paper/paper.md` | | | [docling](https://github.com/docling-project/docling) | `pip install docling` | `docling paper.pdf --enrich-formula --output out/` | `out/paper.md` | Without `--enrich-formula`, every formula becomes ``. Only display formulas are recognized; inline math stays plain text | All of them download ML models on first run, their CLIs change between versions (check `--help` if a flag is rejected), and their licenses differ. If the Markdown still contains a parser's placeholder for a dropped formula or image (``, ``), `convert.py` warns: re-extract with the flag the warning names before translating. For documents with inline math, use MinerU or Marker: docling keeps display formulas only, and `convert.py` warns when it finds several display formulas but no inline math. YAML front matter (`title`, `author`, `lang`) fills `config.txt` and is not sent for translation; without it, a leading `#` heading becomes `original_title`. The temp dir is named after the Markdown file, so `paper.md` maps to `paper_temp/`. If that dir was built from `paper.pdf`, `convert.py` aborts on the source-fingerprint mismatch, so delete it first. `--strip-page-numbers` and `--detect-page-numbers` only apply to Calibre input. At build time Pandoc renders `$...$` / `$$...$$` as MathML, so formulas are typeset in `book.html` and `book.pdf`, and in `book.epub` on readers that support MathML. Calibre's DOCX output cannot typeset MathML: formulas appear there as flattened text followed by their TeX source. ### Step 1.5: Glossary (term consistency across chunks) Each chunk is translated by a fresh-context sub-agent, which means the same proper noun can drift across multiple translations on a 100-chunk book. To fix this, the skill builds a glossary before translation: 1. Sample 5 chunks (first, last, 3 evenly-spaced middle). 2. Extract proper nouns and recurring domain terms; pick canonical translations. 3. Write `/glossary.json` (hand-editable schema below). 4. Run `python3 scripts/glossary.py count-frequencies ` to populate per-term frequencies (ASCII terms use word-boundary regex so `cat` doesn't match `category`; CJK terms use substring; single-CJK-char terms are rejected; aliases count toward the term they belong to). 5. For each chunk, the orchestrator calls `python3 scripts/glossary.py print-terms-for-chunk chunkNNNN.md` and injects the resulting 3-column (`原文 | 别名 | 译文`) markdown table into that chunk's prompt as a hard constraint. Term selection = (terms whose source OR any alias appears in this chunk) ∪ (top-N most-frequent book-wide). ```json { "version": 2, "terms": [ {"id": "Manhattan", "source": "Manhattan", "target": "曼哈顿", "category": "place", "aliases": [], "gender": "unknown", "confidence": "medium", "frequency": 12, "evidence_refs": [], "notes": ""} ], "high_frequency_top_n": 20, "applied_meta_hashes": {} } ``` Existing v1 `glossary.json` files are auto-upgraded to v2 on first load. v2 forbids the same surface form (source or alias) appearing in two different terms; if a v1 file has polysemous duplicate sources, the upgrade aborts with a disambiguation message — fix the file by hand and reload. Edit `glossary.json` between runs to fix translations; existing `glossary.json` is never overwritten — delete it to rebuild from scratch. `scripts/run_state.py` records which glossary terms each chunk used, so later glossary changes (including `target`, `category`, and `aliases` edits) only re-translate affected chunks after the state has been recorded. ### Step 2: Translate (parallel subagents) The skill launches subagents in batches (default: 8 concurrent). Each subagent: 1. Reads one source chunk (e.g. `chunk0042.md`) 2. Translates to the target language 3. Uses a per-chunk term table and short read-only previous/next excerpts 4. Writes the result to `output_chunk0042.md` 5. Writes `output_chunk0042.meta.json` observations for glossary feedback Before launching subagents, `scripts/run_state.py plan ` decides which chunks need translation, which existing outputs only need state recording, and which are unchanged. Use `--retranslate-untracked` only when adopting an old temp dir whose existing outputs should be forced through the current glossary. If a run is interrupted, re-running skips chunks that already have valid output files and current state. Failed chunks are retried once automatically. ### Step 3: Merge & Build ```bash python3 scripts/merge_and_build.py --temp-dir book_temp --title "translated title" ``` Optional output flags: ```bash python3 scripts/merge_and_build.py --temp-dir book_temp --title "translated title" --cover cover.jpg --export-name "translated-title" ``` `--title` becomes the metadata title that readers show in page headers, so pass it without 书名号 or quotes (a wrapping `《》` is stripped). `--cover` passes an explicit image to the EPUB Calibre step. `--export-name` creates alias copies such as `translated-title.epub` while preserving the canonical `book.*` pipeline artifacts. The name `book_doc` (case-insensitive) is reserved and rejected before building because its HTML alias would overwrite `book_doc.html`. Before merging, the script validates: - Every source chunk has a corresponding output file (1:1 match) - Source chunk hashes match the manifest (no stale outputs) - No output files are empty, blank (whitespace-only), or unreadable — a blank chunk aborts the merge instead of silently dropping its content - Every output chunk keeps its source chunk's footnote markers (`[^N]` and `[^N]:`), so no reference or note is left dangling Then: merge → Pandoc HTML → inject TOC → Calibre generates DOCX, EPUB, PDF. Intermediate files stay in the temp dir after the build, so a few bad passages can be fixed without re-translating the book. Either edit the affected `output_chunkNNNN.md` and run `python3 scripts/run_state.py record chunkNNNN`, or delete the file and re-run the skill to re-translate it. `record` marks the chunk as matching the current glossary and source, so run `python3 scripts/run_state.py plan ` first: if that chunk is queued for re-translation because the glossary or its source changed, apply those changes in your edit or re-translate it instead. If the source chunk itself was edited, re-run `convert.py` first so `manifest.json` records the change; otherwise the merge stops with "Source changed since splitting". Leave out page-number flags such as `--strip-page-numbers` on that re-run: once chunks exist they abort, and deleting the cached files as the error suggests would discard the chunks. A re-run may also queue other chunks whose glossary terms changed after they were translated; the skill asks before re-translating those. Then re-run `merge_and_build.py`: it re-merges when a chunk is newer than `output.md` and regenerates the outputs. Do not edit `output.md` itself — any later re-merge rebuilds it from the chunks. `--cleanup` permanently deletes `chunk*.md`, `output_chunk*.md`, and `input.*`, which rules such fixes out; use it only when you are done with the book. **Note:** `{book_name}_temp/` is a working directory for a single translation run. If you change the title, author, output language, template, or image assets, either use a fresh temp directory or delete the existing final artifacts (`output.md`, `book*.html`, `book.docx`, `book.epub`, `book.pdf`) before re-running. ## Project Structure | File | Purpose | |------|---------| | `SKILL.md` | Agent skill definition — orchestrates the full pipeline | | `.claude-plugin/marketplace.json` | Plugin marketplace manifest for Claude Code and GitHub Copilot CLI (single plugin, source `./`) | | `scripts/convert.py` | PDF/DOCX/EPUB → Markdown chunks via Calibre HTMLZ; Markdown input skips Calibre | | `scripts/manifest.py` | Chunk manifest: SHA-256 tracking and merge validation | | `scripts/glossary.py` | Glossary management: per-chunk term tables for consistent terminology | | `scripts/chunk_context.py` | Read-only previous/next chunk excerpts for sub-agent prompts | | `scripts/meta.py` | Per-chunk sub-agent observation file schema (`output_chunkNNNN.meta.json`) | | `scripts/merge_meta.py` | Batch-boundary merge: sub-agent observations → canonical glossary | | `scripts/run_state.py` | Selective re-translation planner and `run_state.json` recorder | | `scripts/merge_and_build.py` | Merge chunks → HTML → DOCX/EPUB/PDF | | `scripts/calibre_html_publish.py` | Calibre wrapper for format conversion | | `scripts/template.html` | Web HTML template with floating TOC | | `scripts/template_ebook.html` | Ebook HTML template | | `tests/baselines/` | Checked-in baseline book inputs for full-pipeline testing | | `tests/.artifacts/` | Ignored full-pipeline test outputs | ## Troubleshooting | Problem | Solution | |---------|----------| | `Calibre ebook-convert not found` | Install Calibre and ensure `ebook-convert` is in PATH | | `Manifest validation failed` | Source chunks changed since splitting — re-run `convert.py` | | `was created from different source bytes` | The temp dir belongs to a different source file — delete the temp dir or use a fresh `--temp-root` | | PDF formulas/tables garbled after conversion | Extract the PDF with a parser from the table in [Step 1](#step-1-convert), delete the old temp dir, and run `convert.py` on the `.md` | | `formula(s) were not decoded` / `image(s) were exported as placeholders` | The parser dropped that content — re-extract with the flag the warning names, delete the temp dir, and run `convert.py` again | | `display formula(s) but no inline math` | The parser turned inline math into plain text (docling's standard pipeline does) — re-extract with MinerU or Marker, delete the temp dir, and run `convert.py` again. If the document has no inline math, ignore it | | `pandoc left N formula(s) as raw TeX` | pandoc could not parse that LaTeX, so the formula shows as `$$...$$` text — fix it in the `output_chunk*.md` holding the snippet the warning prints, then run `merge_and_build.py` again | | `Blank output` / `Empty output` | A subagent wrote a whitespace-only or empty chunk — re-run the skill to re-translate it | | `Missing source chunk` | Source file deleted — re-run `convert.py` to regenerate | | Incomplete translation | Re-run the skill — it resumes from where it stopped | | A few passages need fixing after the build | Fix the affected `output_chunkNNNN.md` instead of `output.md`, then re-run `merge_and_build.py` (see [Step 3](#step-3-merge--build)) | | Changed title/template/assets but output didn't update | Delete existing `output.md`, `book*.html`, `book.docx`, `book.epub`, `book.pdf` from the temp dir, then re-run `merge_and_build.py` | | Want page-number footers stripped from PDF output | For PDF input, monotonic page-number sequences (e.g. `1, 2, 3, ...`) are auto-detected and dropped while outliers like years (`1984`), chapter numbers, and citation indices stay preserved. EPUB and DOCX keep every standalone number, because their page numbers are not text (EPUB anchors, DOCX footers); pass `--detect-page-numbers` for an EPUB that does print page numbers as text. If detection misses your case, pass `--strip-page-numbers` to `convert.py` to aggressively delete every standalone-digit line. Both flags abort if a cached `input.md` or `chunk*.md` already exists — delete them first so the flag actually takes effect. | | `output.md exists but manifest invalid` | Stale output — the script auto-deletes and re-merges | | `Glossary upgrade rejected: duplicate source` | v2 disallows two terms sharing a source/alias surface form. Edit `glossary.json` to disambiguate (e.g., rename one source from `Apple` to `Apple (Inc.)`) and reload. | | PDF generation fails | Ensure Calibre is installed with PDF output support | ## Roadmap [Issue #7](https://github.com/deusyu/translate-book/issues/7) — name/term inconsistency and pronoun/gender errors across chunks — was closed in June 2026, and Phases 1–3 have shipped. The pipeline now covers high-frequency entities, alias/spelling drift, adjacent-chunk pronoun context, and selective re-translation after glossary changes. Full-book organic validation remains a future quality pass. The plan is four independently shippable phases. ### Design principles - **Scripts do bookkeeping; LLMs do semantic merge.** State, schemas, dedup, hashing, IO are deterministic Python. Naming, gender attribution, alias judgment, conflict resolution are LLM calls. - **Single writer for shared state.** Only the main agent writes `glossary.json` and `run_state.json`; sub-agents write per-chunk meta files. No locking needed. - **Conservative merge.** New entities require evidence; alias merges need LLM judgment, not just string similarity; gender starts at `unknown` and only moves up under explicit evidence; canonical values aren't silently overwritten on conflict. - **Three-layer state, three separate files.** `glossary.json` (canonical, sub-agents read), `output_chunkNNNN.meta.json` (raw per-chunk observations), `run_state.json` (orchestration). ### Phase 1 — Sub-agent feedback + glossary merge (shipped) Closes the read+write loop. Glossary v2 adds `id`, `aliases`, `gender`, `confidence`, `evidence_refs`, `notes` (v1 files auto-upgrade on first load; the term table is now 3-col and aliases participate in selection). Sub-agents emit `output_chunkNNNN.meta.json` alongside each translated chunk. `scripts/merge_meta.py` (`prepare-merge` / `apply-merge` / `status`) merges per-batch with conservative rules: surface-form uniqueness enforced, malformed metas quarantined (warn + skip + count), confidence escalation via both `evidence_chunks` and `used_term_sources`, FIFO-cap at 5. See SKILL.md Step 4 / Step 4.5 / Step 5. ### Phase 2 — Neighbor context for pronouns (shipped) `scripts/chunk_context.py` injects `prev_excerpt` (last ~300 chars of previous chunk) and `next_excerpt` (first ~300 chars of next chunk) into each sub-agent prompt as read-only context. No new state files are introduced. ### Phase 3 — Selective re-translation (shipped) Phase 1's batch feedback only improves *forward*. Selective rerun closes the *backward* loop with `scripts/run_state.py` and `run_state.json`: per-chunk tracking of `glossary_version_used`, `entity_ids_used`, `output_hash`, source hash, and selected entity hashes; five planning rules cover missing/empty output, manifest source drift, untracked outputs, source drift since record, and glossary term selection/hash changes. ### Phase 4 — Bootstrap warm-up (experimental, gated on Phase 1 data) Phase 1 grows the glossary batch-by-batch, so the first batch sees the smallest glossary and has the highest drift risk. Possible approaches: sequential bootstrap, variable concurrency, or skip entirely. Decision belongs to whoever has run the system on real books. > Phase 4 remains gated on real-book evidence. The shipped schemas can still evolve under compatibility-aware migrations if production runs expose gaps. ### Parallel track — Pipeline / UX backlog (partly shipped, separate from issue #7) Recent PR discussions also surfaced several useful workflow improvements, but these are broader than one-off patches and touch repo contracts (artifact names, temp-dir behavior, cleanup semantics, or EPUB compatibility scope). Current status: - **Explicit EPUB cover support (shipped).** `merge_and_build.py --cover ` passes the image through the HTML -> EPUB Calibre step. `--cover-from ` / EPUB cover auto-extraction remains out of scope until the project is ready to own EPUB parsing compatibility across different package layouts. (context: closed #3) - **Configurable temp workspace location (shipped).** `convert.py --temp-root ` keeps the default cwd-local `{book_name}_temp/` behavior unless explicitly overridden. (context: closed #4) - **Safer Calibre/Pandoc artifact cleanup (partly shipped).** Page-number and Calibre-marker cleanup is regression-tested, preserving years, chapter numbers, and non-monotonic standalone numbers. Continue improving cleanup incrementally under tests. readmeHtml:
Rainman Translate Book

![English (current language)](#rainman-translate-book) ![Read in Chinese (中文)](README.zh-CN.md) ![Read in Japanese (日本語)](README.ja.md) ![Project page: translate.dyu.sh/en, a one-page guide](https://translate.dyu.sh/en/)

An Agent Skill for Claude Code, Codex, Cursor, OpenClaw and other Agent Skills–compatible agents that translates entire books (PDF/DOCX/EPUB) into any language using parallel subagents.

<p align="center">

<img src="assets/poster/translate-book-poster-en.jpg" alt="translate-book — a whole book, translated in parallel: split into chunks, translated by 8 parallel sub-agents, verified and merged into a complete book" width="480">

</p>

> Inspired by claude_translater. The original project uses shell scripts as its entry point, coordinating the Claude CLI with multiple step scripts to perform chunked translation. This project restructures the workflow as an Agent Skill for Claude Code, Codex, Cursor, OpenClaw, and other compatible agents, using subagents to translate chunks in parallel, with manifest-driven integrity checks, resumable runs, and multi-format output unified into a single pipeline. As the project structure and implementation differ significantly from the original, this is an independent project rather than a fork.

---

How It Works


Input (PDF/DOCX/EPUB)

  │

  ▼

Calibre ebook-convert → HTMLZ → HTML → Markdown

  (or Markdown from a layout-aware PDF parser, skipping Calibre)

  │

  ▼

Split into chunks (chunk0001.md, chunk0002.md, ...)

  │  manifest.json tracks chunk hashes

  ▼

Parallel subagents (8 concurrent by default)

  │  each subagent: read 1 chunk → translate → write output_chunk*.md

  │  batched to respect API rate limits

  ▼

Validate (manifest hash check, 1:1 source↔output match)

  │

  ▼

Merge → Pandoc → HTML (with TOC) → Calibre → DOCX / EPUB / PDF

Each chunk gets its own independent subagent with a fresh context window. This prevents context accumulation and output truncation that happen when translating a full book in a single session.

Features

  • Parallel subagents — 8 concurrent translators per batch, each with isolated context
  • Resumable + selective re-translation — chunk-level resume, with run_state.json tracking glossary-sensitive re-translation
  • Neighbor context — each chunk can see short read-only excerpts from adjacent chunks for pronoun and entity resolution
  • Manifest validation — SHA-256 hash tracking prevents stale or corrupt outputs from being merged
  • Multi-format output — HTML (with floating TOC), DOCX, EPUB, PDF
  • Optional output controls — explicit EPUB cover, custom temp root, and user-facing export aliases
  • Multi-language — any language code, e.g. zh, en, ja, ko, fr, de, es, it (Italian), or one with a region such as zh-TW or pt-BR
  • PDF/DOCX/EPUB/Markdown input — Calibre handles the conversion heavy lifting; formula- and table-heavy PDFs can be pre-extracted to Markdown with a layout-aware parser (see [Step 1](#step-1-convert))

Prerequisites

  • Agent runtime — any agent that supports Agent Skills and can launch sub-agents from a skill (see [Compatibility](#compatibility))
  • Calibre — ebook-convert command must be available (download)
  • Pandoc — for HTML↔Markdown conversion (download)
  • Python 3 with:

- pypandoc — optional (pip install pypandoc); without it the pandoc binary is called directly

- beautifulsoup4 — optional, for better TOC generation (pip install beautifulsoup4)

  • A layout-aware PDF parser — optional, only to pre-extract formula- and table-heavy PDFs to Markdown; supported parsers are listed in [Step 1](#step-1-convert)

Quick Start

1. Install the skill

Any Agent Skills–compatible agent


npx skills add deusyu/translate-book

The command asks which agents to install the skill for. To install it globally for one agent, pass -a <agent> -g, for example npx skills add deusyu/translate-book -a cursor -g:

| -a | Installed to |

|------|--------------|

| claude-code | ~/.claude/skills/translate-book |

| codex, cursor, gemini-cli, opencode, github-copilot | ~/.agents/skills/translate-book (shared) |

| antigravity | ~/.gemini/config/skills/translate-book |

| openclaw | ~/.openclaw/skills/translate-book |

Or install it manually:


mkdir -p ~/.agents/skills

git clone https://github.com/deusyu/translate-book.git ~/.agents/skills/translate-book

Codex, Cursor, Gemini CLI, OpenCode, and GitHub Copilot read ~/.agents/skills/. For Claude Code, clone into ~/.claude/skills/translate-book instead. Restart the agent if the newly installed skill does not appear.

Plugin marketplace (Claude Code, GitHub Copilot CLI)

In Claude Code:


/plugin marketplace add deusyu/translate-book

/plugin install translate-book@translate-book

In GitHub Copilot CLI:


copilot plugin marketplace add deusyu/translate-book

copilot plugin install translate-book@translate-book

Install the skill either as a plugin or into a skills directory, not both: an agent that finds both copies loads both. In Claude Code, the plugin's skill is invoked as /translate-book:translate-book.

OpenClaw


openclaw skills install @deusyu/translate-book

2. Translate a book

Codex

In the Codex CLI or IDE extension, enter:


$translate-book Translate /path/to/book.pdf into Chinese.

Codex can also select the skill automatically when your request matches its description.

Other agents

Ask the agent:


translate /path/to/book.pdf to Chinese

In Claude Code and Cursor, you can also use the slash command:


/translate-book translate /path/to/book.pdf to Japanese

In OpenCode, mention @translate-book in the request.

The skill handles the full pipeline automatically — convert, chunk, translate in parallel, validate, merge, and build all output formats.

3. Find your outputs

All files are in {book_name}_temp/:

| File | Description |

|------|-------------|

| output.md | Merged translated Markdown |

| book.html | Web version with floating TOC |

| book.docx | Word document |

| book.epub | E-book |

| book.pdf | Print-ready PDF |

Compatibility

The skill needs an agent that can launch sub-agents from a skill, one per chunk. If the agent cannot, the skill says so and stops instead of translating the whole book in a single context.

| Agent | Status | Invoke |

|-------|--------|--------|

| Cursor | Verified | /translate-book, or describe the task |

| Claude Code | Original host; minimal test not yet re-run | /translate-book (plugin install: /translate-book:translate-book), or describe the task |

| Codex | Verified | $translate-book, or describe the task |

| OpenClaw | Original host; minimal test not yet re-run | Describe the task |

| Antigravity | Installable, not yet verified | Describe the task |

| Gemini CLI | Installable, not yet verified | Describe the task |

| OpenCode | Installable, not yet verified | @translate-book, or describe the task |

| GitHub Copilot | Installable, not yet verified | Describe the task |

"Verified" means the agent passed this minimal test. Install the skill, then convert a baseline book that ships with it:


S=~/.agents/skills/translate-book   # the skill's install directory

mkdir -p /tmp/tb-smoke && cd /tmp/tb-smoke

python3 "$S/scripts/convert.py" "$S/tests/baselines/diligent-dick/diligent-dick.epub" --olang zh

Then ask the agent:


Use the translate-book skill. Do not convert again; the temp directory is /tmp/tb-smoke/diligent-dick_temp. Only handle chunk0045 and chunk0046, concurrency=2, skip the glossary step, launch one sub-agent per chunk as in Step 4 of SKILL.md to translate them into Chinese, and stop when done.

The agent passes when all three hold:

1. The transcript shows python3 /absolute/path/scripts/chunk_context.py …, so {baseDir} was resolved to a real path.

2. The write times of diligent-dick_temp/output_chunk0045* and output_chunk0046* overlap with the other sub-agent's run, so the chunks were translated in parallel rather than one after another by the main agent.

3. python3 "$S/scripts/merge_meta.py" status diligent-dick_temp reports malformed_meta_files: 0.

Ran it on an agent that is not marked Verified? Please open an issue with the agent, its version, and the three results.

Full-Pipeline Baseline Example

cd tests/.artifacts

Pipeline Details

Step 1: Convert


python3 scripts/convert.py /path/to/book.pdf --olang zh

Calibre converts the input to HTMLZ, which is extracted and converted to Markdown, then split into chunks (~6000 chars each). A manifest.json records the SHA-256 hash of each source chunk for later validation, and a source_fingerprint.json ties the temp dir to the exact source bytes it was built from — re-running against a replaced source file aborts instead of silently reusing stale chunks. Temp dirs created before fingerprinting are adopted with a warning on first re-run.

The HTML → Markdown step also cleans Calibre's markup structurally. EPUB footnotes — a marker link such as <a href="#n1"><sup>1</sup></a> in the text, paired with a note paragraph that opens with a link back to it — become Pandoc footnotes ([^1] in the text, [^1]: … right after the paragraph), numbered across the whole book so that per-chapter numbering cannot collide after merging. In-book links keep their text, span attributes such as {lang="…"}, empty page anchors, and heading ids are dropped, and typographic dashes and quotes stay as Unicode instead of --- or escaped ASCII quotes. Notes without a back-link (for example EPUB 3 <aside> footnotes) stay ordinary paragraphs.

By default the working directory is {book_name}_temp/ under the current directory. Use --temp-root /path/to/work to keep the same leaf directory name under a different parent.

Formula- and table-heavy PDFs: convert Markdown instead (optional)

Calibre reflows PDF text by coordinate heuristics. That works for plain prose, but academic and technical PDFs lose their structure: formulas break into fragments, tables flatten into one cell per line, and multi-column pages interleave. For those PDFs, extract them with a layout-aware parser first and give convert.py the Markdown it writes. .md / .markdown input skips Calibre entirely:


mineru-kit parse paper.pdf -o paper.md          # or any parser from the table below

python3 scripts/convert.py paper.md --olang zh

Any parser works if its Markdown follows these conventions:

  • Formulas as $...$ / $$...$$ LaTeX. Display-math blocks are never split across chunks.
  • Tables as Markdown pipe tables or HTML <table>.
  • Images as files in the Markdown file's directory or its subdirectories, or inlined as base64 data URIs. convert.py copies or decodes them into {book_name}_temp/images/, so chunks never carry image payloads. An image whose path leads outside that directory (through .., an absolute path, or a symlink) is not copied: convert.py warns and leaves the reference as it is.

| Parser | Install | Extract | Markdown file | Notes |

|---|---|---|---|---|

| MinerU >= 4 | pip install -U "mineru>=4.0,<5" | mineru-kit parse paper.pdf -o paper.md | paper.md | CPU-only basic tier: ~0.8 GB of models |

| Marker | pip install marker-pdf | marker_single paper.pdf --output_dir out/ | out/paper/paper.md | |

| docling | pip install docling | docling paper.pdf --enrich-formula --output out/ | out/paper.md | Without --enrich-formula, every formula becomes <!-- formula-not-decoded -->. Only display formulas are recognized; inline math stays plain text |

All of them download ML models on first run, their CLIs change between versions (check --help if a flag is rejected), and their licenses differ. If the Markdown still contains a parser's placeholder for a dropped formula or image (<!-- formula-not-decoded -->, <!-- image -->), convert.py warns: re-extract with the flag the warning names before translating. For documents with inline math, use MinerU or Marker: docling keeps display formulas only, and convert.py warns when it finds several display formulas but no inline math.

YAML front matter (title, author, lang) fills config.txt and is not sent for translation; without it, a leading # heading becomes original_title. The temp dir is named after the Markdown file, so paper.md maps to paper_temp/. If that dir was built from paper.pdf, convert.py aborts on the source-fingerprint mismatch, so delete it first. --strip-page-numbers and --detect-page-numbers only apply to Calibre input.

At build time Pandoc renders $...$ / $$...$$ as MathML, so formulas are typeset in book.html and book.pdf, and in book.epub on readers that support MathML. Calibre's DOCX output cannot typeset MathML: formulas appear there as flattened text followed by their TeX source.

Step 1.5: Glossary (term consistency across chunks)

Each chunk is translated by a fresh-context sub-agent, which means the same proper noun can drift across multiple translations on a 100-chunk book. To fix this, the skill builds a glossary before translation:

1. Sample 5 chunks (first, last, 3 evenly-spaced middle).

2. Extract proper nouns and recurring domain terms; pick canonical translations.

3. Write <temp_dir>/glossary.json (hand-editable schema below).

4. Run python3 scripts/glossary.py count-frequencies <temp_dir> to populate per-term frequencies (ASCII terms use word-boundary regex so cat doesn't match category; CJK terms use substring; single-CJK-char terms are rejected; aliases count toward the term they belong to).

5. For each chunk, the orchestrator calls python3 scripts/glossary.py print-terms-for-chunk <temp_dir> chunkNNNN.md and injects the resulting 3-column (原文 | 别名 | 译文) markdown table into that chunk's prompt as a hard constraint. Term selection = (terms whose source OR any alias appears in this chunk) ∪ (top-N most-frequent book-wide).


{

  "version": 2,

  "terms": [

    {"id": "Manhattan", "source": "Manhattan", "target": "曼哈顿",

     "category": "place", "aliases": [], "gender": "unknown",

     "confidence": "medium", "frequency": 12,

     "evidence_refs": [], "notes": ""}

  ],

  "high_frequency_top_n": 20,

  "applied_meta_hashes": {}

}

Existing v1 glossary.json files are auto-upgraded to v2 on first load. v2 forbids the same surface form (source or alias) appearing in two different terms; if a v1 file has polysemous duplicate sources, the upgrade aborts with a disambiguation message — fix the file by hand and reload.

Edit glossary.json between runs to fix translations; existing glossary.json is never overwritten — delete it to rebuild from scratch. scripts/run_state.py records which glossary terms each chunk used, so later glossary changes (including target, category, and aliases edits) only re-translate affected chunks after the state has been recorded.

Step 2: Translate (parallel subagents)

The skill launches subagents in batches (default: 8 concurrent). Each subagent:

1. Reads one source chunk (e.g. chunk0042.md)

2. Translates to the target language

3. Uses a per-chunk term table and short read-only previous/next excerpts

4. Writes the result to output_chunk0042.md

5. Writes output_chunk0042.meta.json observations for glossary feedback

Before launching subagents, scripts/run_state.py plan <temp_dir> decides which chunks need translation, which existing outputs only need state recording, and which are unchanged. Use --retranslate-untracked only when adopting an old temp dir whose existing outputs should be forced through the current glossary. If a run is interrupted, re-running skips chunks that already have valid output files and current state. Failed chunks are retried once automatically.

Step 3: Merge & Build


python3 scripts/merge_and_build.py --temp-dir book_temp --title "translated title"

Optional output flags:


python3 scripts/merge_and_build.py --temp-dir book_temp --title "translated title" --cover cover.jpg --export-name "translated-title"

--title becomes the metadata title that readers show in page headers, so pass it without 书名号 or quotes (a wrapping 《》 is stripped). --cover passes an explicit image to the EPUB Calibre step. --export-name creates alias copies such as translated-title.epub while preserving the canonical book.* pipeline artifacts. The name book_doc (case-insensitive) is reserved and rejected before building because its HTML alias would overwrite book_doc.html.

Before merging, the script validates:

  • Every source chunk has a corresponding output file (1:1 match)
  • Source chunk hashes match the manifest (no stale outputs)
  • No output files are empty, blank (whitespace-only), or unreadable — a blank chunk aborts the merge instead of silently dropping its content
  • Every output chunk keeps its source chunk's footnote markers ([^N] and [^N]:), so no reference or note is left dangling

Then: merge → Pandoc HTML → inject TOC → Calibre generates DOCX, EPUB, PDF.

Intermediate files stay in the temp dir after the build, so a few bad passages can be fixed without re-translating the book. Either edit the affected output_chunkNNNN.md and run python3 scripts/run_state.py record <temp_dir> chunkNNNN, or delete the file and re-run the skill to re-translate it. record marks the chunk as matching the current glossary and source, so run python3 scripts/run_state.py plan <temp_dir> first: if that chunk is queued for re-translation because the glossary or its source changed, apply those changes in your edit or re-translate it instead. If the source chunk itself was edited, re-run convert.py first so manifest.json records the change; otherwise the merge stops with "Source changed since splitting". Leave out page-number flags such as --strip-page-numbers on that re-run: once chunks exist they abort, and deleting the cached files as the error suggests would discard the chunks. A re-run may also queue other chunks whose glossary terms changed after they were translated; the skill asks before re-translating those. Then re-run merge_and_build.py: it re-merges when a chunk is newer than output.md and regenerates the outputs. Do not edit output.md itself — any later re-merge rebuilds it from the chunks. --cleanup permanently deletes chunk*.md, output_chunk*.md, and input.*, which rules such fixes out; use it only when you are done with the book.

Note: {book_name}_temp/ is a working directory for a single translation run. If you change the title, author, output language, template, or image assets, either use a fresh temp directory or delete the existing final artifacts (output.md, book*.html, book.docx, book.epub, book.pdf) before re-running.

Troubleshooting

| Problem | Solution |

|---------|----------|

| Calibre ebook-convert not found | Install Calibre and ensure ebook-convert is in PATH |

| Manifest validation failed | Source chunks changed since splitting — re-run convert.py |

| was created from different source bytes | The temp dir belongs to a different source file — delete the temp dir or use a fresh --temp-root |

| PDF formulas/tables garbled after conversion | Extract the PDF with a parser from the table in [Step 1](#step-1-convert), delete the old temp dir, and run convert.py on the .md |

| formula(s) were not decoded / image(s) were exported as placeholders | The parser dropped that content — re-extract with the flag the warning names, delete the temp dir, and run convert.py again |

| display formula(s) but no inline math | The parser turned inline math into plain text (docling's standard pipeline does) — re-extract with MinerU or Marker, delete the temp dir, and run convert.py again. If the document has no inline math, ignore it |

| pandoc left N formula(s) as raw TeX | pandoc could not parse that LaTeX, so the formula shows as $$...$$ text — fix it in the output_chunk*.md holding the snippet the warning prints, then run merge_and_build.py again |

| Blank output / Empty output | A subagent wrote a whitespace-only or empty chunk — re-run the skill to re-translate it |

| Missing source chunk | Source file deleted — re-run convert.py to regenerate |

| Incomplete translation | Re-run the skill — it resumes from where it stopped |

| A few passages need fixing after the build | Fix the affected output_chunkNNNN.md instead of output.md, then re-run merge_and_build.py (see [Step 3](#step-3-merge--build)) |

| Changed title/template/assets but output didn't update | Delete existing output.md, book*.html, book.docx, book.epub, book.pdf from the temp dir, then re-run merge_and_build.py |

| Want page-number footers stripped from PDF output | For PDF input, monotonic page-number sequences (e.g. 1, 2, 3, ...) are auto-detected and dropped while outliers like years (1984), chapter numbers, and citation indices stay preserved. EPUB and DOCX keep every standalone number, because their page numbers are not text (EPUB anchors, DOCX footers); pass --detect-page-numbers for an EPUB that does print page numbers as text. If detection misses your case, pass --strip-page-numbers to convert.py to aggressively delete every standalone-digit line. Both flags abort if a cached input.md or chunk*.md already exists — delete them first so the flag actually takes effect. |

| output.md exists but manifest invalid | Stale output — the script auto-deletes and re-merges |

| Glossary upgrade rejected: duplicate source | v2 disallows two terms sharing a source/alias surface form. Edit glossary.json to disambiguate (e.g., rename one source from Apple to Apple (Inc.)) and reload. |

| PDF generation fails | Ensure Calibre is installed with PDF output support |

Roadmap

Issue #7 — name/term inconsistency and pronoun/gender errors across chunks — was closed in June 2026, and Phases 1–3 have shipped. The pipeline now covers high-frequency entities, alias/spelling drift, adjacent-chunk pronoun context, and selective re-translation after glossary changes. Full-book organic validation remains a future quality pass. The plan is four independently shippable phases.

Design principles

  • Scripts do bookkeeping; LLMs do semantic merge. State, schemas, dedup, hashing, IO are deterministic Python. Naming, gender attribution, alias judgment, conflict resolution are LLM calls.
  • Single writer for shared state. Only the main agent writes glossary.json and run_state.json; sub-agents write per-chunk meta files. No locking needed.
  • Conservative merge. New entities require evidence; alias merges need LLM judgment, not just string similarity; gender starts at unknown and only moves up under explicit evidence; canonical values aren't silently overwritten on conflict.
  • Three-layer state, three separate files. glossary.json (canonical, sub-agents read), output_chunkNNNN.meta.json (raw per-chunk observations), run_state.json (orchestration).

Phase 1 — Sub-agent feedback + glossary merge (shipped)

Closes the read+write loop. Glossary v2 adds id, aliases, gender, confidence, evidence_refs, notes (v1 files auto-upgrade on first load; the term table is now 3-col and aliases participate in selection). Sub-agents emit output_chunkNNNN.meta.json alongside each translated chunk. scripts/merge_meta.py (prepare-merge / apply-merge / status) merges per-batch with conservative rules: surface-form uniqueness enforced, malformed metas quarantined (warn + skip + count), confidence escalation via both evidence_chunks and used_term_sources, FIFO-cap at 5. See SKILL.md Step 4 / Step 4.5 / Step 5.

Phase 2 — Neighbor context for pronouns (shipped)

scripts/chunk_context.py injects prev_excerpt (last ~300 chars of previous chunk) and next_excerpt (first ~300 chars of next chunk) into each sub-agent prompt as read-only context. No new state files are introduced.

Phase 3 — Selective re-translation (shipped)

Phase 1's batch feedback only improves *forward*. Selective rerun closes the *backward* loop with scripts/run_state.py and run_state.json: per-chunk tracking of glossary_version_used, entity_ids_used, output_hash, source hash, and selected entity hashes; five planning rules cover missing/empty output, manifest source drift, untracked outputs, source drift since record, and glossary term selection/hash changes.

Phase 4 — Bootstrap warm-up (experimental, gated on Phase 1 data)

Phase 1 grows the glossary batch-by-batch, so the first batch sees the smallest glossary and has the highest drift risk. Possible approaches: sequential bootstrap, variable concurrency, or skip entirely. Decision belongs to whoever has run the system on real books.

> Phase 4 remains gated on real-book evidence. The shipped schemas can still evolve under compatibility-aware migrations if production runs expose gaps.

The entry MUST include the original `kind` and (for `conflicting_new_entity_proposals`) the `variants` array, so apply-merge can validate and act: ```json {"id": "d1", "kind": "alias", "variant": "Taig", "candidate_source": "Tai", "choice": "yes_alias"} ``` 6. Write the decisions JSON, `{"auto_apply": [...], "decisions": [...], "consumed_chunk_ids": [...]}`, to `/merge_decisions.json` with your file-writing tool, replacing the previous batch's file. Its entity names and evidence quotes are book text, so apply-merge reads the file on stdin instead of taking the JSON in the command (see "Book Text and the Shell"): ```bash python3 {baseDir}/scripts/merge_meta.py apply-merge "" < "/merge_decisions.json" ``` Surface the summary JSON (`auto_applied`, `decisions_resolved`, `consumed_chunks`, `errors`) in your batch progress message. **apply-merge is transactional.** If any decision is malformed (wrong choice for kind, missing fields, references a non-existent entity), the entire batch aborts with a non-zero exit and stderr details — no glossary mutation, no hashes recorded. On non-zero exit, fix the offending decision in `merge_decisions.json` and run the command again; `prepare-merge` will surface the same proposals because nothing was consumed. **Decision order in the input list is not significant.** `apply-merge` internally dispatches entity-creating decisions before alias-attaching ones, so `yes_alias` decisions whose candidate is created by another decision in the same batch (a `use_standalone_N`, `use_variant_N`, or `promote_to_separate_entity`) succeed regardless of the order you pass them in. Alias chains (e.g. `Taighi → Taig` where `Taig → Tai` is also a pending alias decision) resolve via a fixed-point loop within the alias-attacher pass — you don't need to topo-sort or sequence chained aliases manually. On a fresh run after a previous interrupted batch, `prepare-merge` will pick up any meta files left behind. Don't manually delete them. ### 5. Verify Completeness and Retry After all batches complete, use Glob to check that every source chunk has a corresponding output file. If any are missing, retry them — each missing chunk as its own sub-agent. Maximum 2 attempts per chunk (initial + 1 retry). Also read `manifest.json` and verify: - Every chunk id has a corresponding output file - No output file is empty (0 bytes) or blank (whitespace-only) Check the heading structure of the whole book, since each chunk was translated in isolation and headings decide the EPUB/PDF table of contents. This lists every heading of the output chunks in book order, leaving out `#` lines inside code blocks: ```bash python3 {baseDir}/scripts/merge_and_build.py --temp-dir "" --headings ``` Look for chapters split into two headings (a bare number heading followed by the title heading), the same kind of unit at different levels (one chapter `#`, the next `##`), and back-matter sections nested under the index. Fix them in the `output_chunk*.md` files and record each edited chunk (see the **Edit** path in Step 9). Also look at front and back matter carried over from the source edition, which no longer fits the translated book: a printed contents list copied from the source (the reader builds its own TOC), a "page numbers follow the print edition" accessibility note, and an index whose page numbers refer to the print edition. Tell the user what you found and remove or annotate it only with their agreement. Then run the meta-merge observability snapshot: ```bash python3 {baseDir}/scripts/merge_meta.py status "" ``` Also run the selective re-translation state snapshot: ```bash python3 {baseDir}/scripts/run_state.py status "" ``` Surface a one-line summary in the verification report: > Translated chunks: 50 • Meta files: 48 found / 47 consumed • Malformed: 1 (chunk0099 — see stderr) • Chunks missing meta: chunk0017, chunk0042 Severity rules (none of these fail the run — meta is non-blocking): - `unmerged_meta_files > 0` after Step 4.5 ran → bug, flag prominently. Resume should have caught this. - `malformed_meta_files > 0` → sub-agent emitted invalid meta; print chunk_ids and a "fix the file by hand and re-run if you want this chunk's feedback merged" note. - `meta_files_found < translated_chunks` → sub-agent-compliance issue (some chunks didn't emit meta at all). Print missing chunk_ids. Report any chunks that failed translation after retry. ### 6. Translate Book Title Read `config.txt` from the temp directory to get the `original_title` field. If it is missing (e.g. Markdown input with neither front matter nor a leading `#` title) or is just the source file name (Calibre falls back to it for PDFs without title metadata, e.g. `1706.03762`), read the start of `chunk0001.md`: if it clearly shows the document's title, use that; otherwise use the source file name. Translate the title to the target language. If the book has a published translation, use its title (ask the user, or search for it) rather than a literal translation. Pass the bare title, without 书名号 or quotes: it becomes the EPUB/DOCX/PDF metadata title, which readers show in page headers and the library (`merge_and_build.py` strips a wrapping `《》` anyway). ### 7. Post-process — Merge and Build Write the translated title to `/title.txt` and the export name to `/export_name.txt` with your file-writing tool, then run the build script. The command reads both from those files instead of quoting them (see "Book Text and the Shell"): ```bash python3 {baseDir}/scripts/merge_and_build.py --temp-dir "" --title "$(cat "/title.txt")" --export-name "$(cat "/export_name.txt")" ``` `--export-name` adds copies of every output named after the book (`.epub`, ...) next to the canonical `book.*` files, which the pipeline keeps using internally. Use the user's `export_name` if given, otherwise the translated title with characters that are invalid in file names removed. If the user provided `epub_cover`, add `--cover ""`. The build skips outputs that already exist. To rebuild after changing the title, author, language, or cover, first delete `book.html`, `book_doc.html`, `output.html`, `book.docx`, `book.epub`, `book.pdf` and the export copies from the temp dir; otherwise the old metadata stays inside the files even though the file names change. Keep the intermediate files. The chunks, `manifest.json`, and `run_state.json` are what make spot fixes and selective re-translation possible after the build (see Step 9). Add `--cleanup` only when the user explicitly asks to delete intermediates, and tell them first that it permanently deletes `chunk*.md`, `output_chunk*.md`, `input.html`, and `input.md`: after that, fixing a single chunk means converting and translating the whole book again. The script reads `output_lang` from `config.txt` automatically. Optional overrides: `--lang`, `--author`. An author goes through a file too: `--author "$(cat "/author.txt")"`. This produces in the temp directory: - `output.md` — merged translated markdown - `book.html` — web version with floating TOC - `book_doc.html` — ebook version - `book.docx`, `book.epub`, `book.pdf` — format conversions (requires Calibre) ### 8. Report Results Tell the user: - Where the output files are located - How many chunks were translated - The translated title - List generated output files with sizes - Any format generation failures - Any `pandoc left N formula(s) as raw TeX` warning with the formulas it lists; those show as LaTeX source in the book and can be fixed as in Step 9 - That the intermediate files are kept so passages can still be fixed (Step 9), and that they can ask for cleanup once they are done with the book Do not run `--cleanup` as part of this report. Offer it only after the user says they expect no more edits, and before running it, say what it deletes (see Step 7). Re-running the Step 7 build command with the same flags plus `--cleanup` keeps the existing outputs and then deletes the intermediates; if any format fails, the script skips cleanup and keeps them. ### 9. Spot Fixes After the Build If the user finds problems in a few places after the build, fix the affected chunks rather than `output.md`: whenever a chunk changes, the build re-merges `output.md` from the chunks and discards edits made there. 1. Find the chunk: search `/output_chunk*.md` for the passage. The passage is book text: use your file-search tool, or put it in a file and run `grep -F -f "" ""/output_chunk*.md` (see "Book Text and the Shell"). 2. Either edit `output_chunk.md` directly with your file-editing tool, or have it re-translated. **Edit.** `record` stamps the chunk as matching the current source and glossary, so first check what the planner still expects from it: ```bash python3 {baseDir}/scripts/run_state.py plan "" ``` If chunk appears in `chunks[]` with action `translate`, recording would hide that. Handle it by reason: - `glossary_term_hash_changed` (its `detail` lists the term ids) or `glossary_term_selection_changed`: bring those terms in line with `glossary.py print-terms-for-chunk "" "chunk.md"` in the same edit. - `manifest_source_hash_changed`: the source chunk was edited after splitting. Re-run the Step 2 `convert.py` command first, leaving out page-number flags such as `--strip-page-numbers`: once chunks exist, those flags abort and suggest deleting the cached files or the whole temp dir, which would also delete the translations. Without them it keeps the existing chunks and writes their new hashes to `manifest.json`. Skip this and the merge stops with "Source changed since splitting" even after re-translating. Plan again: the chunk is then queued with `source_hash_changed_since_record`. - `source_hash_changed_since_record` or any other reason: re-translate the chunk instead of editing it. Then record the edited output: ```bash python3 {baseDir}/scripts/run_state.py record "" chunk ``` **Re-translate.** Delete `output_chunk.md` and run Steps 3.7–4.5 again. The planner re-checks the whole book, so `translation_chunk_ids` can also list chunks the user did not mention, typically ones whose glossary terms changed after they were translated (`glossary_term_selection_changed` or `glossary_term_hash_changed` in the plan's `chunks[].reasons`). Translate only the chunks the user asked for; if the plan lists others, show the user those chunk ids with their reasons and ask before re-translating them. 3. Re-run the Step 7 build command with the same flags. It re-merges because the chunk is newer than `output.md`, then regenerates the HTML and the other formats.
